clue.text: Rambling hikers miss engagements

indicators.note: rambling talk wanders without order, so the following words lose their sequence and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Walkers out on a ramble fail to turn up for their appointments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rambling hikers' reads as a natural pair, but 'Rambling' is the signal to rearrange; 'engagements' looks like diary dates, but here it means fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Skirmishes are small military clashes, and an engagement in military language is a battle or fight.

clue.text: Gloomy busker's ending with nothing in hat

parts.note: sombre means dark or gloomy

indicators.note: the ending of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: the final letter of busker
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A miserable street musician has collected nothing in his hat.
explanation.walkthrough: A busker is a street performer who plays for coins tossed into a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a broad-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Jubilant hearts lift after start of seasonal occasion in pub

indicators.note: everything before sits in the drinking place, which wraps around it

parts.note: an inn is a pub

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces follows the second, so they join in that order
the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of seasonal
an event is an occasion
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
to heave is to lift something heavy

explanation.surface: People at a festive party in the local feel their spirits rise.
explanation.walkthrough: Note the order: the clue gives 'hearts lift' first, but 'after' puts it behind the seasonal occasion, and the pub's letters split to hold the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in seventh heaven is an idiom for being blissfully happy, a state of utmost joy.

clue.text: Average spell

definitions.meaning: a verb, to signify, as in 'this will spell trouble'

explanation.walkthrough: 'spell' suggests a period of time or magic; here it is the verb meaning signify.
explanation.definitionFit: A mean is the statistical average, and to mean is to signify, as when letters spell a word.

clue.text: One made to take blame in a case got badly broken by pressure

indicators.note: a word broken by another is split apart with that letter inserted
done badly means done wrongly, so the letters come out in a muddled order

parts.note: taken as written
P is the symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: A defendant cracked under pressure in a trial and was made to carry the blame.
explanation.definitionFit: A scapegoat is a person unfairly forced to bear responsibility for the wrongdoing of others.

clue.text: Record in moment erased

indicators.note: the letters needed are contained within the following words, running across their join

parts.note: the letters sit across the two words

explanation.surface: A recording made at some moment has been wiped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' is the verb here, as in writing details into a ledger.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter data or details in a book is to record them, as clerks do in a register.

clue.text: Race about in south of France

indicators.note: one word sits in the other, so its letter goes inside the longer word

parts.note: sud is the French word for south
C is short for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone dashes around the Riviera or elsewhere in southern France.
explanation.walkthrough: 'south of France' tempts a solver toward S for south; it actually asks for the French word for south.
explanation.definitionFit: To scud is to move fast and smoothly, as clouds driven by wind do, so it can mean to race.

clue.text: Some more chat, too confused, had adverse consequences

indicators.note: confused words are jumbled up, so the preceding letters are put into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone muddled by extra chatter suffered the fallout.
explanation.definitionFit: When chickens come home to roost, past misdeeds return to cause trouble, which is the idiom's meaning of bad results catching up.

clue.text: Cut up, start to exhibit resolve

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: food that is cut into cubes is diced

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: the first letter of exhibit

explanation.surface: Someone, upset at being chopped from an exhibition, makes up their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut up' looks like a single phrase meaning upset; 'up' is separate, turning the word over.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide and to resolve both mean to settle firmly on a course of action.

clue.text: Blemish covered by mother with a cosmetic

indicators.note: something covered by another thing is enclosed by it, so the first word sits inside the second

parts.note: an informal word for mother
'with' joins on the letter a, taken as written
a scar is a mark on the skin

explanation.surface: A mark on the face is hidden by Mum using some make-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' tacks the final letter on outside the mother, after the blemish has gone inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is a make-up product applied to darken and thicken the eyelashes.

clue.text: Bear followed by timid animals endlessly symbolic

indicators.note: without an end, so the last letter of the word before it is dropped
one part is placed after the other, so the pieces join in the order given

parts.note: to tote is to carry or bear
mice are proverbially timid creatures

explanation.surface: A bear is trailed by some nervous little creatures, in a scene that seems full of meaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bear' looks like the animal, matching 'animals' later, but it is the verb to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: A totem is an emblem standing for a clan or idea, so totemic describes something serving as an emblem.

clue.text: Old, upset, taken in by trick producing negative balance

indicators.note: something taken in by another is held inside it

parts.note: a trap is a trick to catch someone

indicators.note: upset means turned over, which in a down entry flips the word upside down

parts.note: aged means old

explanation.surface: An elderly person, distressed, is conned and ends up in debt.
explanation.walkthrough: The flipped word goes between the A and P of the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade gap is a deficit when a country's imports exceed its exports, a negative balance of trade.

clue.text: Wander in crowd, having day off

indicators.note: the abbreviation for day is taken off, so that letter goes from the word for a crowd

parts.note: a drove is a large moving crowd, of animals or people
D is the abbreviation for day

explanation.surface: Someone takes a day off and drifts about among the crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word here: the definition is 'Wander' and the wordplay follows.
explanation.definitionFit: To rove is to roam about aimlessly, an exact synonym of wandering.

clue.text: Criticised copy, hurt

parts.note: a repro is a reproduction
past tense of ache, to hurt

explanation.surface: Someone was criticised for copying, and it stung.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to express disapproval of them, so reproached matches criticised as a past-tense verb.

clue.text: Report slug at home

parts.note: slug is slang for a bullet
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: A sighting of a garden slug is reported from the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slug' suggests the garden pest; it is slang for a gun's projectile.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulletin is a short official news report or statement.

clue.text: Horrid to fans, our side lost enthusiasm

indicators.note: something horrid is a mess, so the next three words are scrambled

parts.note: taken as written
a side is a team in sport

explanation.surface: Our team, rude to its own supporters, played without spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: To run out of steam is to become tired and stop trying, as a steam engine slows when its fuel is spent.

clue.text: Suspect something is wrong with lines in defamation followed by rising cheers

indicators.note: the next piece is placed after the first, so they join in order
the lines go inside the word for slander, splitting it

parts.note: a smear is a damaging slander
L is the abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means read from bottom to top

parts.note: ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: An actor feels uneasy about lines in a libellous script that the audience then cheers.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is everyday British slang for thank you, much as cheers is; in a down entry 'rising' reads it bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: To smell a rat is an idiom for sensing that something is fishy or a trick is being played.

clue.text: Renegade erred, set adrift

indicators.note: something adrift floats loose out of position, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rebel went wrong and was cast loose at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A deserter abandons their side or cause, as a renegade turns traitor to theirs.

clue.text: Important step from fellow in ballet that he adapted

indicators.note: one thing is placed within the others, so its letter goes among them
something adapted is altered in form, so the collected letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dancer adapts a ballet, and the result is a key move in his career.
explanation.walkthrough: F can go anywhere among the other letters, since the whole lot is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says that getting started, or knowing something, is half the battle: a large part of the success.

clue.text: Agent bearing remedy

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
an air is a person's manner or bearing

explanation.surface: A spy carrying a cure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' looks like 'carrying'; it is the noun meaning manner.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair something is to fix it, the verb sense of remedy, putting a fault right.

clue.text: Level with trade union colleague in the end

parts.note: even means level or flat
TU is the abbreviation for trade union
an ally is an associate or partner

explanation.surface: Someone finally draws level with a fellow union member.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventually means after some time or at last, the same sense as finally arriving at the end.

clue.text: Stadium in China renamed

indicators.note: the letters are contained within the next words, spanning their join

parts.note: the letters sit across the two words

explanation.surface: A sports ground in China has been given a new name.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is an enclosed venue for sport or entertainment, much as a stadium is.

clue.text: Genuine regret after time

indicators.note: the second word is placed following the first, so time's letter comes first

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: Someone feels real remorse once time has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: True and genuine both describe something real and authentic rather than fake.

clue.text: Theory supplied by assistant, first to last

indicators.note: the opening letter is moved round to the end of the word

parts.note: an aide is an assistant

explanation.surface: A notion put forward by a helper.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a notion or hypothesis, as a theory is a proposed explanation.

clue.text: Further loan

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to promote or help along
second meaning: a noun, money paid before it is due or lent

explanation.walkthrough: 'Further loan' reads as a second loan; split it into a verb and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance a cause is to further it, and an advance is a sum of money lent or paid early.

clue.text: New cadet or old soldier?

indicators.note: a new version of the letters means they are made over into a different order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Is this a fresh recruit or a veteran? The question mark flags the playful turn.
explanation.walkthrough: Redcoat was the name for a British soldier of past centuries, from the scarlet uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: British infantry once wore red tunics, so a redcoat is a soldier of former times.

clue.text: Clear about nitrogen outside

indicators.note: one word goes around the other, so it surrounds the chemical symbol

parts.note: to rid is to clear of something
N is the chemical symbol for nitrogen

explanation.surface: Someone sweeps nitrogen away from the open air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' looks like a positional instruction, but it is the definition, a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A rind is the tough outer skin of fruit or cheese, the outside layer.

clue.text: Stamp designed by flower expert

indicators.note: a design rearranges elements into a new pattern, so the letters before it are reordered

parts.note: taken as written
an aster is a daisy-like garden flower

explanation.surface: A postage stamp has been designed by someone who specialises in flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' simply places the flower after the rearranged letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A past master is a person highly skilled in an activity, a seasoned expert.
